case_summary.text: IT/ILT : Where ITES segment of a company was similar to that of assessee-company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs, but there was discrepancy in annual report and in information gathered under section 133(6), said company could not have been taken as comparable
Co. outsourcing major portion of its business to third party couldn't be taken as comparable for ITES provider

IT/ILT: Where assessee was a captive ITES service provider, while comparable company was engaged in software development activities as well as ITES and there was no segmental data for ITES sector and, hence, no feasible financial comparison as against that of assessee-company was possible, said company was to be excluded from list of comparables

IT/ILT: In case of assessee rendering ITES services to AE, a company engaged into providing IT and ITES whereas no segmental information was available in its annual report, was not acceptable as comparable

IT/ILT: Where assessee was rendering ITES services to AE, a company having substantial 'other income' which was about 48 per cent of total revenue, and segmental details of which were not available, could not be accepted as comparable
IT/ILT: Where comparable was engaged in IT, ITES and sale of products for which segmental information was not available, no comparison could be made for want of segmental data

IT/ILT : Where assessee was providing ITES services to AE, a company which outsourced major portion of its work and thereby failed to satisfy employee cost to sales filter, could not be accepted as comparable

IT/ILT: Where assessee was rendering software development services to AE, a company dealing with software testing, software development services and healthcare services about which no separate segmental data was available, could not be accepted as comparable
IT/ILT : Where assessee was providing ITES services to AE, a company which outsourced substantial portion of its work, was not acceptable as comparable
IT/ILT : Where assessee was rendering ITES service to AE, company which outsourced major portion of its business, could not be accepted as comparable

IT/ILT : Where assessee was rendering software development services to AE, a company in whose case segmental information containing break-up of its export sales and employee cost was not available and, thus, it was not possible to ascertain if it passed export earnings and/or employee costs filters, same could not be accepted as comparable
IT/ILT: In case of assessee rendering ITES services to AE, a company which had outsourced its significant work to outside ventures, was not acceptable as comparable
IT/ILT : Where assessee was rendering ITES services to AE as captive service provider, a company which outsourced major portion of its work, could not be accepted as comparable

IT/ILT: Where assessee was captive ITES service provider while comparable company was engaged in software development and no segmental data was available, said company was to be excluded from list of comparables

IT/ILT: In case of assessee rendering ITES services to AE, a company providing services of medical transcription and consultancy and which outsourced a major portion of translation work to third parties, was not acceptable as comparable
Company with insignificant ITeS segment turnover not a valid comparable due to extreme scale mismatch: HC

IT/ILT : Where company had treated data cleansing services and software development services as a single segment and segmental information was not available, it should be excluded from comparability analysis

IT/ILT: Where assessee was providing software development services to AE, a company which was engaged in software development and also in ITES segment, and seperate segmental data for software development services was not available, could not be accepted as comparable
Co. providing consultancy in business solution is incomparable with ITES in absence of segmental data
IT/ILT : In case of assessee rendering ITES services to AE, a KPO company which outsourced substantial portion of its work, was not acceptable as comparable

IT/ILT : In case of assessee providing software development services to AE, a company which was rendering both software development services and ITES services but break-up of revenues from those two segments was not available, was not acceptable as comparable

IT/ILT: Where assessee was rendering software development services to AE, a company earning revenue from three segments namely software services, software products and other services about which segmental information was not available, was not acceptable as comparable
IT/ILT: Where assessee-company was providing ITeS itself while comparable company outsourced significant part of its activities, they could not be compared
IT/ILT : Companies outsourcing considerable portion of their business to third party vendor unlike assessee, could not be taken as comparable
IT/ILT: In case of assessee rendering ITES services to AE, a company which followed different business model as it outsourced its work to external vendors, was not acceptable as comparable

IT/ILT : Where assessee was providing BPO services to AEs and employees cost was 62 per cent of total cost of services, whereas in company selected as comparable employee cost was less than 2 per cent which indicated that most of work was outsourced, company was to be excluded from list of comparables
IT/ILT-I: In case of assessee, rendering ITES services to its AE, a company which significantly outsourced its activities, could not be accepted as comparable
ITES & SDS segments to be aggregated for benchmarking purpose in absence of authenticated figures revenue of cost

IT/ILT: Where was rendering technical support and maintenance services to its AE, a company engaged in various activities such as sale of software licence, software services, export, revenue from subscription etc. about which no segmental information was available, could not be accepted as comparable

IT/ILT : In case of assessee rendering software development services to AE, a company engaged in both ITES services and software development services about which segmental information was not available, could not be accepted as comparable

TRANSFER PRICING : A company engaged in diversified IT services, including analytics and consulting, and lacking reliable segmental data to isolate SDS segment, was functionally incomparable to assessee, a captive software development service provider and was to be excluded from set of comparables

IT/ILT: A company incurring expenses to extent of 23 per cent on outsourcing of medical transcription activity, being involved in a different functional model was incomparable to assessee mainly providing IT enabled services and software development services

IT/ILT: Where assessee was ITES service provider whose functions are purely back end office support services of data management while comparable company provided both technical services and ITES service and it had association with companies having higher brand value impacting profitability, it could not be a comparable company

TRANSFER PRICING : Where assessee was engaged in providing ITES and Commissioner (Appeals) suo motu excluded a company on ground that there was no reliable segmental information with respect to its ITES segment, since functions performed by said company was comparable to ITES provided by assessee, issue was to be remitted to TPO/Assessing Officer to verify segmental details

TRANSFER PRICING : In case of assessee engaged in providing ITES services to AE, a company rendering various services such as software development and maintenance, software testing, infrastructure set-up and management, consulting service, architecture, configuration and installation, etc., about which segmental information was not available, was not acceptable as comparable

IT/ILT: Where assessee was rendering technical support and maintenance services to its AE, a company engaged in various activities such as sale of software licence, software services, export, revenue from subscription etc. about which no segmental information was available, could not be accepted as comparable
Co. outsourcing significant part of its operations can't be a comparable for a Co. rendering IT enabled services

TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company had earned revenue from information technology/BPO related services and sales from infra activities, due to non-availability of reliable segmental data, selected company could not be considered to be comparable to assessee, rendering ITE services
IT/ILT: Where company outsourced most of its work to third party vendors, it could not be selected as comparable
ITAT justified exclusion of comparables as segmental data of software development services wasn’t available

IT/ILT : Where assessee-company was rendering software development services to AE, a company which apart from earning income form software services, also earned income from 'Business process outsourcing services', which fell in realm of IT enabled services and there was no segmental information qua software services alone, said company could not be accepted as comparable

IT/ILT: Where assessee had business in two segments and in respect of selection of comparable companies for ITES segment, issue of functional comparability and employee cost filter was raised but same was not ascertained, matter was to be remanded
IT/ILT: Where assessee rendered ITES services to AE, a company which developed its own software and a company which outsourced its significant work, could not be accepted as comparables
IT/ILT: A company which outsourced its work to sub-vendors as against assessee carrying out its activities in-house, could not be selected as comparable

IT/ILT: A KPO company involved in diverse nature of services and having no segmental data for diversified service portfolio, would not be comparable to assessee engaged in providing BPO services to its AEs

IT/ILT : In case of assessee rendering software development services to AE, a company earning revenue from software development services as well as sale of software products about which segmental data was not available, could not be accepted as comparable

IT/ILT : Where assessee, a 100 per cent EOU, was providing ITES services to its AE, a company which failed to satisfy 75 per cent export sale filter adopted by DRP, could not be included as comparable

IT/ILT : Where ITES activities of a company included data centre management services, end user computing services, managed security services, which were not functionally similar to that of assessee company providing IT enabled services to its AE, said company had to be excluded from final list of comparables
Companies with significantly higher turnover than ITES segment of assessee to be excluded in TP comparables:ITAT

IT/ILT: In case of assessee rendering software development services to AE, a company engaged in product development, software development and ITES, about which segmental details were not available, could not be acceptable as comparable

Infosys BPO Ltd. It is amongst the top 10 third party BPO company in India. As the company is in the BPO services, it cannot be compared with the assessee who is engaged in ITES services. Delhi High Court in case of Rampgreen Solutions (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2015] 60 taxmann.com 355/234 Taxman 573/377 ITR 533 had held that ITES companies and BPO companies are not comparable. Therefore, following the decision of Delhi High Court, this comparable is excluded. [Para 19]

Crossdomain Solutions (P.) Ltd.

In view of the decision of Delhi High Court in Rampgreen Solutions (P.) Ltd.'s case (supra) where the functional profile of company is very high end KPO services, it cannot be compared with the assessee and, hence, this comparable is directed to be excluded. [Para 24]

It is also seen that the annual report of this company does not contain segment wise result in the case of ITeS and technical services and, therefore, in absence of segment wise results, it cannot be accepted as a comparable.

Comparable TCS-E Serve International Ltd. This company is engaged in providing diversified services which included ITeS and technical services like software testing, verification, data processing services and validation of software at the time of implementation and data centre management activities and, therefore, this company is not functionally comparable to the ITeS segment of the assessee. It is further seen that the annual report of this company also did not contain segmental details in the case of ITeS and technical services. This company was directed to be excluded as a comparable. [Para 5]

However, on the basis of the working submitted by the TPO it shows that segmental revenue of Rs. 979 crores which is for the reasons stated with respect to exclusion of Infosys BPO squarely applies to this comparable also. consideration that primarily the company is not engaged in software development and it was engaged in providing IT enabled services (ITes) only. The technical services of software testing, verification and validation of the software were carried out at the time of implementation of software only and are in the nature of back-office support. On perusal of the service agreement between 'CDS' and the assessee, the assessee was also engaged in application development and support, web development etc. [Para 6.5] In view of the comparison of the services rendered by the assessee and the services rendered by the company, the company cannot be rejected on the ground of functional dissimilarity. [Para 6.7]

Further, the contention of revenue to exclude the company on the ground of non-availability of segment information is also not tenable as the company was functioning in one segment of ITES only.

The contention of the revenue for exclusion on the ground of deemed RPT is also not acceptable. With effect from 1-1-2009, the Tata consultancy services Ltd. is the holding company of the company and thus during the entire period under consideration i.e. 1-4-2009 to 31-3-2010, the transactions with Citigroup Companies cannot be held as related party transactions in the case of the company. The assessee has not brought on record any evidence that the assessee-company continued to provide services to the city group companies on the basis of agreements contracted prior to 1-1-2009. Even if, the services were provided under a long-term contract, still it cannot be deemed a related party transaction in view of the change of ownership. [Para 6.9]

Further, the contention of the revenue of impact of 'Tata' brand on profitability of the company is also not tenable in view of the facts that no evidence has been brought on record as to how the 'Tata' brand has impacted the profitability of the company. Further, the expenditure corresponding to contribution to 'Tata' brand by the company, is also very small part (0.43 per cent) of the total operational expenses of the company. [Para 6.10]

In view of the above discussion, the finding of the DRP in retaining TCS E-serve International Ltd. in the set of comparables is upheld. [Para 6.11]

Comparable TCS E-Serve Ltd.

On perusal of the annual report of the company, it is found that it has rendered services identical to the services rendered by TCS E-serve International Ltd.

Thus, the activities of the company are identical to the activities of TCS E-serve International Ltd., which are held to be in the nature of ITes and functionally similar to the assessee. Accordingly, the company cannot be excluded on the ground of functional dissimilarity. [Para 7.2]

The arguments of the revenue on the issue of non-availability of segment information, deemed related party transactions and entity having access to Tata brand are identical to the arguments taken in the case of TCS e-serve International Ltd. Thus following the find in the case of comparable TCS e-serve international Ltd. The direction of the DRP in retaining, TCS e-serve limited as a valid comparable is upheld. [Para 7.4]

Comparable Accentia Technology Ltd.

In assessment year 2009-10 in the case of the assessee itself, the company has been excluded by the Tribunal. On the ground of lack of segment information of various streams of income and events of acquisition of companies. In the year under consideration also the income derived by the company is from various streams including medical transcription; Billings and collection, income from coding etc. and no segmental information of each of the streams are available. Similarly, the company has itself mentioned in the annual report that due to acquisitions of companies during the year, its results were not comparable with the earlier year. [Para 8.6]

Thus, in view of the identical facts during the year under consideration, respectfully following the decision of the Tribunal in assessment year 2009-10, said company cannot be included in the set of comparables and accordingly, the Assessing Officer/TPO should exclude it from the set of comparables. [Para 8.7]

Comparable Infosys BPO Ltd.

The Annual Report of the company showed that it was established in April, 2002 as the business process outsourcing subsidiary of the Infosys technologies Ltd. The annual report further mentioned that it is among the top 10 third-party BPO company in India according to the ranking of National Association of Software and Service Companies (NADDCOM). Thus, the contention of the revenue that the company provided wide array of the services, is not relevant as far as the function of BPO carried out by the company are similar to the functions carried out by the assessee. When, the assessee itself has characterized its activity as BPO, in such circumstances, the functions of the company cannot be held as the dissimilar. [Para 9.2]

35]

Comparable Company Accentia Technology

Considering the decision of the Tribunal in Willis Processing Services (India) Ltd. (supra), wherein it was held that this comparable company is engaged in developing software product and rendering medical transcription services and cannot be compared with the assessee engaged in providing back office support services. Further, extraordinary events took place during the year which has an impact on its financials. Therefore, this comparable is directed to be excluded. [Para 36]

Comparable Company I Services The Delhi Tribunal in Dy. CIT v. Everest Business Advisory India (P.) Ltd. [2018] 89 taxmann.com 323 (Delhi - Trib.) for the same assessment year held that the business profile of I Services shows that it is into high-end diversifying services vis-a-vis the taxpayer who is into divergent high-end services like web hosting, e-mail services, spam filtering, domain names and DNS hosting, web hosting, e-mail services and directed to exclude from comparing with IT enabled services. Therefore, considering the decision of the Delhi Tribunal, the exclusion of I Services is to be directed. [Para 37]

Comparable Company Coral Hubs (Vishal Information)

In the case of Willis Processing Services (India) (P.) Ltd. (supra) on comparability, the Tribunal held that the company Coral Hub (earlier known as Vishal Information Technology) had a business model where services are outsourced, as against the business model of the assessee where services are rendered by employing own employees and using one's own infrastructure, and on this basis it can safely be concluded that the said comparable was functionally different, and as such was liable to be excluded from the final list of comparables. [Para 38]

Considering the decision of the Tribunal on similar submission, exclusion of Coral Hubs (Vishal Information) from the list of comparables is to be directed. [Para 39]

Comparable Company Cosmic Global

Considering the fact that major part of the income of this comparable is from translation charges and function of this comparable is different from the assessee-company, exclusion of Cosmic Global from the list of comparables is to be directed. Similar view was taken by the Pune Tribunal in BNY Mellon International Operations (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy.CIT [2015] 55 taxmann.com 386 (Pune - Trib.) holding that this comparable company had outsourced its vendor and was making high vendor payments as compared to sales and, hence, was not comparable. [Para 41]

Comparable Company Informed Technologies

The co-ordinate bench in Stream International Services (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2015] 53 taxmann.com 19/152 ITD 664 (Mum. - Trib.) while considering the similar ground for exclusion on the ground of low cost employee compared to the assessee held that where employee cost to sale is 27.77 per cent as compared to that of the assessee which is 49.34 per cent, this comparable was directed to be excluded. Therefore, considering the decision of the Tribunal, this comparable is also directed to be excluded. [Para 43]

Comparable Company Maple Solutions and Triton Corp.

The Mumbai Tribunal in Stream International Services (P.) Ltd. (supra) held that a company under serious indictment in fraud cases is to be excluded from the list of comparables on the ground of unreliability of data. Thus, following the order of the Tribunal, this company is to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Paras 45 and 46]

Comparable Company ICRA Techno Analytics

The Delhi Court in Pr. CIT v. BC Management Services (P.) Ltd. [2018] 89 taxmann.com 68/253 Taxman 138/403 ITR 45 while considering the comparability of ICRA Techo Analytics, held that a company providing consultancy business solution and testing, and high-end BPO services, in absence of segmental data, not comparable with ITES. The TPO rejected the assessee's TP Report/Study and conducted his own search process adopting various criteria/filters and selected 10 companies as the final set of comparables. In the instant appeal, the assessee contended exclusion and inclusion of certain companies.

HELD: Comparable companies Universal Print System, Infosys BPO, BNR Udyog, TCS E- serve and Excel Infoways

It is to be seen that the Co-ordinate Bench of the Tribunal in the case of Mobily Infotech India (P.) Ltd., v. Dy. CIT [2018] 97 taxmann.com 2 (Bang. - Trib.) has considered and adjudicated on the comparability of the above 5 companies with companies rendering ITES. It is to be found that the functional profile of that company i.e., Mobily Infotech India (P.) Ltd. is similar to that of the assessee and the assessment year is also the same, viz., assessment year 2012-13. It is seen that the TPO has selected the same set of comparables in both; Mobily Infotech India (P.) Ltd., (supra) as well as in the instant case. Since the facts and circumstances are similar, the decision rendered by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Tribunal in the case of Mobily Infotech India (P.) Ltd., (supra) applicable to the facts of the instant case. The relevant portion of the aforesaid decision of the Co-ordinate Bench (supra) thereof are extracted hereunder:-

Universal Print Systems (Seg. BPO)

The Tribunal held that on similar facts, as in the case on hand a co-ordinate bench of the Tribunal in the case of CGI Information Systems and Management Consultants (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2019] 101 taxmann.com 294 has remanded the issue of comparability analysis at the segmental level to the file of the TPO for examination and verification by holding that this company has four segment viz., Repro, Label Printing, Offset Printing and Pre-press BPO. Comparable Vitae International Accounting Services Pvt. Ltd.

■

The contention of the assessee that the said company is engaged in accounting, auditing and bookkeeping services is to be accepted. These activities are clearly distinct from the routine ITES/DCM services rendered by the assessee. Further, the company does not provide reliable segmental information to carve out margins relating to comparable services. In view of the functional dissimilarity and lack of segmental data and following the decision of the Hyderabad Tribunal in Infor (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [IT(TP)A No. 1341 (Hyd.) of 2024, dated 5-5-2025], it is to be held that Vitae International Accounting Services Pvt. Ltd. cannot be considered as a valid comparable and is liable to be excluded. [Para 36.1]

Comparables Domex E-Data Pvt. Ltd., Lagnaum Infotech Solutions Pvt. Ltd. and Brickworks India Pvt. Ltd.

■

With regard to Domex E-Data, Lagnaum Infotech Solutions and Brickworks India, it is noted that these companies are engaged in knowledge-based and analytics-driven services. The TPO himself has categorised the assessee's DCM segment as ITES. As per Rule 10TA(e) and 10TA(g) of the Incometax Rules, ITeS and KPO services are distinct in nature. Companies rendering KPO services, which involve higher skill, domain expertise and value addition, cannot be compared with a routine ITES service provider. It is further noted that Domex E-Data and Brickworks India do not have proper segmental information, and Brickworks India also earns abnormal profits. Lagnaum Infotech Solutions shows fluctuating margins over the years. These factors make the margins of these companies unreliable for benchmarking. Accordingly, these three companies are not suitable comparables and deserve to be excluded. [Para 36.2]

Comparable MPS Ltd.

■

It is found that this company is engaged in publishing solutions, digital learning content, platforms and related services. The activities involve content creation, full-service publishing, learning solutions and aggregation of content, which are clearly knowledge-intensive in nature. The Annual Report of MPS for financial year 2019-20 shows diversified operations across multiple verticals. The assessee, on the other hand, is a routine ITES service provider rendering low-end services. Therefore, MPS Ltd. fails the functional comparability test prescribed under Rule 10B of the Income Tax Rule. It is also note that there is no reliable segmental information available to isolate margins relatable to ITES activities. In similar facts, the Hyderabad Tribunal in Infor (India) (P.) Ltd. (supra) has held MPS is not comparable with an ITES provider. Following the same, the exclusion of MPS from the final set of comparables is directed. [Para 36.3]

■

In view of the above discussion, it is held that Vitae International Accounting Services, Domex E-Data, Lagnaum Infotech Solutions, MPS and Brickworks India are not comparable to the assessee in the DCM/ITeS segment. The Assessing Officer/TPO is directed to exclude these companies from the final list of comparables and recompute the arm's length price accordingly. Thus, the ground raised by the assessee on this issue is allowed. [Para 36.4]

FACT: The assessee-company UHG India was into providing IT Enabled Health care services to UHG Group companies as a captive service provider. The assessee had two segments concerning international transactions viz. Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES) and Software Development services. In its Transfer Pricing Study the assessee used TNMM as Most Appropriate Method (MAM) for both the segments and computed its margin at 13.83 per cent and 13.23 per cent in ITES and Software Development services respectively.

The TPO after examining the TP study made by the assessee and on the basis of various filters, made its own TP analysis by selecting 8 comparables for ITES segment and 18 comparables in software development segment and calculated their margin at 34.29 per cent and 28.88 per cent respectively and computed the cumulative adjustment in both the segments.

The DRP gave partial relief by excluding Bodhtree Consulting, CAT Technologies and Aricent Technologies from the final set of comparables qua software development services and by excluding Coral Hub qua ITES segment for benchmarking the international transaction.

On appeal to the Tribunal the assessee sought exclusion of 5 comparables and 3 comparables qua software development services and ITES segment respectively and also sought inclusion of 3 comparables qua ITES segment. The revenue also challenged exclusion of Bodhtree, CAT Technology qua software development segment and Coral Hub in ITES for benchmarking the international transaction.

Cosmic Global Limited

From the material on record it is apparent that outsourcing charges of this case constitute 57.31 per cent of the total operating costs. This does not appear to be a valid reason for eliminating this case from the list of comparables. On going through the Annual accounts of Cosmic Global Limited, it is found that its total revenue from operations are at Rs.7.37 crore divided into three segments, namely, Medical transcription and consultancy services at Rs.9.90 lakhs, Translation charges at Rs.6.99 crore and Accounts BPO at Rs.27.76 lakhs. The assessee has made out a case that outsourcing activity carried out by this company constitutes 57 per cent of total expenses.

When one is examining the results of this company from the Accounts BPO segment alone, there is no need to examine the position under other segments. The entire outsourcing is confined to Translation charges paid at Rs.3.00 crore, which is strictly in the realm of the Translation segment, revenues from which are to the tune of Rs.6.99 crore. If this segment of Translation is not under consideration for deciding as to whether this case is comparable or not, one cannot take recourse to the figures which are relevant for segments other than accounts BPO. Thus it is held that this case cannot be excluded on the strength of outsourcing activity, which is alien to the relevant segment. [Para 13.2]

However, this case is found to incomparable on the alternative argument advanced by the assessee to the effect that total revenue of the Accounts BPO segment of Cosmic Global Limited is very low at Rs.27.76 lakhs. A captive unit cannot be compared with a giant case. As the segmental revenue of BPO segment of Cosmic Global Limited at Rs. 27.76 lakh is still on much lower side, this case is, therefore, directed to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 13.3]

On appeal to the Tribunal: HELD: On the issue of segmental financials and TP adjustment to be restricted to AE transactions, it is found that the TPO has rejected the segmental profit and loss account given by the assessee and reworked the segmental profit and loss account. The TPO has not given any reason for rejecting the segmental profit and loss account given by the assessee. The assessee has rightly contended that section 92 can be applied only in respect of international transactions, i.e., transactions with AE. In view of the above transfer pricing provisions and various judicial precedents, it is held that the transfer pricing adjustment should be restricted only to the AE related transactions of the assessee. In view of the given facts and circumstances of the case, it would be just and appropriate to set aside the impugned order on this issue and remand the issue to the TPO to verify the segmental profit and loss account given by the assessee. The assessee shall provide all the details including details of allocation in case in support of segmental drawn by it. The TPO shall give proper opportunity of hearing to the assessee. [Para 4.6]

Comparable : Infosys BPO Ltd.

The Bangalore Bench of the Tribunal in the case of Ocwen Financial Solutions (P.) Ltd. v. Jt. CIT [2019] 108 taxmann.com 306, had excluded Infosys BPO Ltd. form the list of comparable company. The relevant finding of the Bangalore Bench of the Tribunal, reads as follows, 'Infosys' offers a gamut of different and diversified services which cannot be compared with routine back office services provided by the assessee. In fact, the company 'Infosys' provides business process management services which are different from routine back office services. It is also seen that this company enjoys significant brand value and owns intangible assets which clearly establish that Infosys is different from the assessee in the case on hand. [Para 6.2.1]

Since the profile of the assessee-company and the profile of the assessee in the case of Ocwen Financial Solutions (P.) Ltd. However, DRP vide its direction dated 17-12-2014 while discussing the above comparable noted that annual report of the company is given to the assessee for the financial year ending on 31-3-2009, instead of 2007, hence, the TPO was directed to provide annual report of March 2007. However, the TPO vide order dated 14-1-2015 giving effect to the order of the DRP has not provided this information and the annual report of the above company was also for June financial year ending and not for March ending. A comparable cannot be included in the comparability analysis for comparing the PLI of the assessee without having concise and precise publicly information about the comparable for same financial period. In the instant case the comparable is following June as its accounting year, therefore, without having publicly available information about the comparable for the comparative accounting year of the assessee it cannot be selected as comparable. In view of this, the above comparable is directed to be excluded solely for the reason of non-availability of comparable financial information.[Para 57]

The observations made by the TPO that Gillanders Arbuthnot & Co. Ltd. is not engaged in the business of turnkey project, is incorrect. From the information given by the said company under the Engineering Division, it is vivid that it is also engaged in the business of projects on turnkey basis. It can further be noticed that the total revenue of this concern from Engineering Division is at Rs. 74.17 crore. The TPO has excluded this case by mentioning that the said company is primarily engaged in man-made cotton fibre yarn and also saleable tea. One fails to appreciate this reason for the exclusion of this case on segment level because the revenue from the Engineering segment is Rs. 74.17 crore, which is much more than the assessee's uncontroverted filter of Rs. 25 crore minimum turnover. The revenue from the Engineering Division may be less in percentage terms on the entity level, but is substantial on the segment level. The segmental results of Engineering Division of Gillanders Arbuthnot & Co. Ltd. should have been included in the list of comparables. First reason is that profit motive is not a relevant consideration in case of Government undertakings. Many Government Undertakings even operate on losses in furtherance of the social obligations of the government. The second reason is that Engineers India Limited earned income from turnkey project by successfully completing the project of IOCL and other Public Sector Undertakings. This shows that the company has a dependency on the technology to deliver the functions. Since the functions performed by the comparable are dependent on the technology and are therefore, not comparable with the tested party. Accordingly, this is not a good comparable in this case. This in view of the proposition of ‘functional similarity’ laid down by the Delhi High Court in the Rampreen Green Solutions. In view of above, there is no infirmity in the action of the Commissioner (Appeals), hence, sane is upheld. [Para 64]

Comparable Quippo Valuers and Auctioneers Pvt. Ltd.

■

The services provided by this company are in the nature of valuation and auctioning, which are different from the assessee. Further, this company has been excluded on the basis of functional comparability by the co-ordinate bench in Adidas Technical Services (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2016] 69 taxmann.com 401 (Delhi - Trib.). Therefore, the decision of the Commissioner (Appeals) to exclude this company from the list of comparables is upheld. [Para 67]

Comparbale TSR Darashaw Ltd.

■

TSR Darashaw Ltd. provides registrar and transfer agent services, records management services and payroll and trust fund services. All these segments are functionally different from the marketing support activities performed by the assessee. Further, this company has been consistently excluded on the basis of functional comparability by the co-ordinate benches and the exclusion is upheld by the High Court. Therefore, the decision of the Commissioner (Appeals) to exclude this company from the list of comparables is upheld. [Para 70]

Comparable India Tourism Development Corporation Ltd. (ITDCL)

■

ITDCL is a government company engaged in operation of hotels, restaurants, shops and also earns revenue from consultancy and ticketing systems. The TPO has observed that the functions performed by Ashok Reservation and Management System (ARMS) are close to the functions performed by the tested party. The segmental data is available in the Annual Report, therefore, ARMS segment of ITDC is a good comparable with the tested party. Therefore, in this background, the Commissioner (Appeals) has rightly directed the Assessing Officer to include ITDS (ARMS segment) as a good comparable if the assessee provides the segmental financial results for benchmarking analysis. In view of above, the action of the Commissioner (Appeals), is upheld. [Para 73]

Comparable Overseas Manpower Corporation Ltd.

■

The Delhi High Court in the case of Chryscapital Investment Advisors (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2015] 56 taxmann.com 417/232 Taxman 20/376 ITR 183 (Delhi) ) has held that the company cannot be rejected merely on account of wide fluctuation in margin (profit/loss) if it is otherwise comparable. It is noted that Commissioner (Appeals) has observed in his finding that TPO has nowhere questioned the functional comparability aspect, and therefore, observed that Overseas Manpower Corporation Limited is a good comparable and directed the Assessing Officer to include it in the final matrix of comparables. In the background of the aforesaid, the action of the Commissioner (Appeals) is upheld. [Para 76]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Segmental results) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Whether where assessee was providing ITES services to its AE, a company engaged in rendering both ITES and software development services having no available segmental data, was not acceptable as comparable - Held, yes [Paras 52 and 56][In favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Knowledge Process Outsourcing (KPO)) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether where assessee was rendering ITES services to AE, a company engaged in Engineering Design Service (CAD/CAM) and Geographical Information System (GIS) which were in nature of KPO services, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes [Para 13] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : Where assessee was rendering ITES services to AE, a company engaged in Engineering Design Service (CAD/CAM) and Geographical Information System (GIS) which were in nature of KPO services, could not be accepted as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING : In case of assessee engaged in providing ITES services to AE, a company rendering various services such as software development and maintenance, software testing, infrastructure set-up and management, consulting service, architecture, configuration and installation, etc., about which segmental information was not available, was not acceptable as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING : Where assessee was rendering ITES services to AE, a company whose financial result for financial year 2008-09 corresponding to financial year followed by assessee was very much available with TPO, could not be excluded from list of comparables merely because it had a different financial year ending  TRANSFER PRICING : In case of assessee engaged in providing ITES services to AE, a company engaged in development and sale of software products about which segmental information was not available, could not be accepted as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING : Where assessee was rendering ITES services to AE, a company which was involved in various segments such as healthcare management services legal process outsourcing services etc. about which segmental information was not available and, moreover, an extraordinary event of amalgamation took place in its case during relevant previous year, could not be accepted as comparable

III. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Adjustments - Employee cost) - Assessment year 2005-06 - Whether a company who outsourced about 44.81 per cent of its business and has a low employee cost of 1.25 per cent of operating revenue and Tribunal has also observed that TPO himself referred to NASSCOM survey that average wages and salaries to sales ratio of IT/ITES industry in India was 46.1 per cent and assessee's wages to sales is 53 per cent then same is not comparable to selected company whose wages to sales is 1.25 per cent only - Held, yes [Para 20] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparability factors - Employee cost filter) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where percentage of outsourced business of selected company had been reported as 44.81 per cent in same assessment year whereas assessee claimed that ratio of outsourcing expenses to total expenses was 65.98 per cent, TPO should verify exact quantum of outsourcing expenses in case of selected company and decide issue of exclusion of said company in accordance with law and after giving adequate opportunity of being heard to assessee - Held, yes [Para 18] [Matter remanded]TRANSFER PRICING : Where percentage of outsourced business of selected company had been reported as 44.81 per cent in same AY whereas assessee claimed that ratio of outsourcing expenses to total expenses was 65.98 per cent, TPO should verify exact quantum of outsourcing expenses in case of selected company and decide exclusion of comparable company in accordance with law and after giving adequate opportunity of being heard to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company having extraordinary event such as merger/demerger could not be compared with assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : When assessee sought to exclude company as being functionally different but TPO had gathered financial and functional details of company by way of using his authority under section 133(6) and included said company as comparable but said information had not been provided to assessee, matter should be restored to file of AO/TPO to decide issue afresh  TRANSFER PRICING : Where data provided by selected company was unreliable due to fraud committed by owner/directors, then said company cannot be held as comparables to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company was having only one segment of Information Technology enabled services and was primarily engaged in field of IT-BPO, AO/TPO should include said company into set of comparables to assessee ITES provider

Ltd. v. Dy. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Assessee provided ITES services whereby raw data comprised of unprocessed or semi-processed data pertaining to business of American Express locations worldwide was received and processed for preparation of various kinds of business, accounting and financial reports - E-Clerx Services was providing end to end support in trade lifecycle including trade confirmation, settlement, transaction maintenance, risk analysis and reporting and most of its activities relates to settlement etc. - Whether functionally E-Clerx Services could not be said to be comparable to assessee - Held, yes - Whether further since E-Clerx Services had significant intangibles being 7.24 per cent of total assets whereas in case of assessee there was none, and E-Clerx outsourced substantial part of its services to third parties while assessee used only its own human resource, E-Clerx would not be comparable - facts.text:
The assessee-company was engaged in the business of ITeS in the field of architectural and interior designing. The assessee had entered into various international transactions with its Associated Enterprises (AEs).

The TPO rejected the assessee's submission and selected comparables in the ITeS segment and arrived at median (5th place) at 23.35 per cent. The Assessing Officer finally made a total adjustment on the international transaction relating to ITeS segment.

The assessee submitted that out of the comparables selected by the TPO, they want exclusion of only one comparable, i.e., Domex e-Data Pvt. Ltd. since the said company was functionally dissimilar as it was engaged in diversified services including software development, Knowledge Process Outsource (KPO), Business Process Outsource (BPO) and further that the segmental details were not available in the annual report.

The assessee, a BPO and a captive service provider, was providing ITE Services to its AEs.

The limited issue for adjudication in the present appeal was with reference to inclusion/exclusion of comparable companies. The assessee was seeking exclusion of, Domex, MPS, Vitae and Access Healthcare on the ground of functional disparity, extraordinary events and non-availability of segmental data.

The assessee-company UHG India was into providing IT Enabled Health care services to UHG Group companies as a captive service provider. The assessee had two segments concerning international transactions viz. Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES) and Software Development services. In its Transfer Pricing Study the assessee used TNMM as Most Appropriate Method (MAM) for both the segments and computed its margin at 13.83 per cent and 13.23 per cent in ITES and Software Development services respectively.

The TPO after examining the TP study made by the assessee and on the basis of various filters, made its own TP analysis by selecting 8 comparables for ITES segment and 18 comparables in software development segment and calculated their margin at 34.29 per cent and 28.88 per cent respectively and computed the cumulative adjustment in both the segments.

The DRP gave partial relief by excluding Bodhtree Consulting, CAT Technologies and Aricent Technologies from the final set of comparables qua software development services and by excluding Coral Hub qua ITES segment for benchmarking the international transaction.

On appeal to the Tribunal the assessee sought exclusion of 5 comparables and 3 comparables qua software development services and ITES segment respectively and also sought inclusion of 3 comparables qua ITES segment. The revenue also challenged exclusion of Bodhtree, CAT Technology qua software development segment and Coral Hub in ITES for benchmarking the international transaction.

The assessee-company was providing infrastructure support IT services as a help desk to cater to the foreign clients of CompuCom, USA.

The assessee objected to the inclusion of a company by stating that it was engaged in dissimilar business, dissimilar employee cost and exceptional high margins. The TPO rejected the assessee's contention of high profit margin by holding that once arithmetic mean of profit margins of the comparables was taken, there remained no net to exclude companies with super profit margins. The TPO, however, did not discuss the other dissimilarities pointed out by the assessee.

The DRP observed that the TPO selected only the 'Prepress-BPO' segment of this company, which was comparable to the ITES activities of the assessee. No relief was, therefore, allowed by the DRP on this count.

The assessee entered into international transactions of provision of contract software development (IT) services and Information Technologies Enabled Services (ITES) to its associated enterprises (AEs). The Profit Level Indicator (PLI) of Operating Profit/Operating Cost (OP/OC) of the assessee-company for the software development services was 14.53 per cent and for ITES segment it arrived at 13.59 per cent.

For benchmarking its international transactions the assessee adopted Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) as Most Appropriate Method (MAM) and selected 8 comparables for software development segment and 11 comparables for ITES segment. The mean of PLI of OP/OC of software development segment was arrived at 13.35 per cent and for ITES segment it arrived at 9.42 per cent. Therefore, the assessee stated that the said transactions was at arm's length.

The TPO stated that the search process of the assessee was flawed because of the inappropriate filters and therefore he concluded fresh search and finally selected 8 new comparables for software development segment whose PLI was 21.30 per cent. Similarly, for the ITES segment, the TPO selected 6 new comparables whose PLI was 17.62 per cent. Accordingly, adjustment was made to the ALP of assessee. Further, there was another adjustment made on account of the interest on outstanding balances of the advance receivables from AE.

On appeal, the DRP granted certain relief to the assessee on adjustment made by the TPO. Interest on overdue receivables was reduced to Rs. 1.4 thousand.

In the instant appeal, the assessee contested the inclusion of Infosys BPO, comparable selected for ITES segment and for software development segment the assessee challenged inclusion of Infosys Technologies. Further, the assessee also contested the adjustment made on account of the interest charged on outstanding receivables.

■

The assessee, a wholly owned subsidiary of a foreign company and a captive provider of ITeS and Software Development Services (SDS) to its AEs, filed its return declaring certain income .

■

The case was selected for scrutiny and referred to the TPO under section 92CA for international transactions in the SDS segment.

■

The TPO proposed a TP adjustment including Mindtree Limited and Nihilent Limited in the final set of comparables; (ii) rejecting DCIS Dot Com Solutions India Pvt. Ltd. and Rheal Software Pvt. Ltd. on the ground that they failed the persistent loss filter because they had losses in two out of the three relevant financial years. The AO issued a draft assessment order proposing to add the TP adjustment.

Comparable Infosys Technologies Ltd.

-paper activities and has only considered the ITES segment.

Before DRP assessee contended that it is earning extraordinary profit, functionally different and has RPT of 38.54 per cent. The DRP rejected the contention of the assessee holding that TPO has taken into consideration only the ITES segment of the comparable. Before Tribunal, it was submitted that the comparable has the unreliable books of account and therefore same should be rejected. It was also submitted that it is functionally different. It is undisputed that the comparable company is also engaged in software development services. However the TPO has obtained information under section 133(6) and after that he has excluded the segmental information pertaining to software development services and has only considered the information pertaining to segment of data cleansing solution. The argument of assessee that it has unreliable books and has applied the accounting concept of matching wrongly is a new argument which was neither before TPO and nor before the DRP. However, the assessee has relied on the decision of co-ordinate bench of Ciena India (P.) Ltd. v. ITO [2015] 59 taxmann 92 (Delhi-Trib) for assessment year 2009-10.

On perusal of said order, it is apparent that co-ordinate benche considered the accounting policy of the comparable with respect to software development services for assessment year 2009-10. However in the present case assessment year involved is 2007-08 and furthermore the segment of the comparable of software development is not at all considered by TPO, he has considered ITES segment of the comparable. Therefore, reliance placed upon the above decision of the co-ordinate bench is misplaced. In view of this the argument of assessee for exclusion of the above comparable is rejected.

Eclerx Services Limited

The assessee submitted that the company is operating in data analytics space and provides operations management, audit and reconciliation service. It was submitted that it falls in the domain of KPO segment. It was further submitted that the company is providing high end services and therefore same should be excluded. For this assessee submitted a corporate presentation of the comparable wherein it is apparent that the company became first KPO in 2008 which is listed on BSE and NSE.

From the above it is apparent that the company is engaged in the KPO business and therefore same is not comparable with the appellant which is carrying on admittedly ITES services. The Delhi High Court in case of Rampgreen Solutions (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2015] 234 Taxman 573/60 taxmann.com 355 has held that KPO segment cannot be compared with ITES segment. Therefore following the decision of the High Court it is directed to exclude this comparable.

Informed Technologies India Ltd.

The assessee raised an objection that the company has an abnormal growth and also low employee cost to sales ratio of 17.79 per cent and therefore it should be excluded. Before DRP also the same argument was taken which was rejected by the DRP. Abnormal growth of the company could not be a ground for rejection of a comparable if it is found to be functionally similar. Hence the contention of the assessee is rejected that because of abnormal growth this comparable should be rejected.

Regarding low cost employees the assessee relied on the decision of C3i Support Services (P.) Ltd. and e4e Business Solutions India (P.) Ltd. However, on consideration of the decision cited above it is found that these decisions did not consider the above comparable at all. Further it is not argued by the assessee that how this company is functionally not comparable with the assessee company as that is the utmost requirement for exclusion or retention of any comparable. Therefore this company has been rightly included as comparable by TPO and the argument of the assessee for its exclusion is rejected.

Infosys BPO Limited and Wipro Limited

The above companies have been selected by TPO as its comparable. However the assessee objected the above comparable that they own intangible and are having brand value. The TPO rejected the above contentions. Before DRP the submission of the assessee was rejected. Wipro Ltd. was also objected on ground that it is engaged in BPO services. It was also submitted that Delhi High Court in case Aginity India Technologies (P.) Ltd. has considered these comparables. Having considered the rival contentions and following the decision of Delhi High Court both these comparables have to be excluded as they have brand value and also own the intangible which are not comparable with the business of the assessee.

Maple E-Solutions Limited

It is undisputed fact that this company has been acquired by Triton Corp Ltd. which has also been taken as comparable by the TPO. As there is an extraordinary event, this company is directed to be excluded as comparable.

Mold-Tek Technologies Limited

The TPO rejected the argument of the assessee. The DRP also confirmed the findings of the TPO however as the assessee is engaged in ITES services and admittedly the comparable is a KPO, both are not functionally comparable. In view of this, the comparable is rejected and its exclusion is directed.

Vishal Information Technologies Limited

The services rendered by Katerra India in the ITeS segment comprises of the outsource work provided to it by the US entity and Katerra India performs such drawings, etc., regarding interior designs and sends the same work done to the AE and the service income is charged by the assessee in lieu of services rendered to the AE. Ltd. showed that in the column of 'technology absorption' it is mentioned that this company has made efforts towards technology absorption meaning thereby, the software development activity is carried out with the usage of very high end software, hardware and the company always uses latest available technology in development of software. Therefore, it is evident that Domex e-Data Pvt. Ltd. is a company engaged in the various activities including software development activity using high end software, hardware and is also involved in products innovation and renovation, so these activities are absolutely dissimilar with ITeS functions performed by the assessee. While it is clear from the TPO's order that if the benchmarking is done only for the medical transcription segment, then the RPT pertaining to that segment only should be considered. However, since how much of the RPT pertain to the medical transcription segment has not been determined by either the TPO or the assessee, it would be appropriate and proper to remand the matter of comparability of this company, to the file of the TPO for determination of the issue afresh. Genesys International Corporation Ltd. The assessee is basically providing various services to the customers of its AEs in relation to human resources which are more or less centered around the employees of the prospective clients. When one consider the nature of services provided by Genesys International Corporation Ltd., it comes to the forefront that they are providing full range of geospatial services to its customers. In simple terms, geospatial services means the services relating to the relative position of things on the earth's surface. These basically include 3D mapping, Navigation maps, Image processing, Cadastral mapping, etc. If one takes into account the nature of services provided by the assessee, being financial and retirement security, health, productivity of employees and employment relationships and then try to compare them with those rendered by Genesys, it is manifested that both are totally incomparable. [Para 14.2]

The TPO has examined CBDT Circular SO. 890 (E) dated 26-9-2000 which provides a detailed list of products or services that can be covered under the ITES for the purposes of sections 10A and 10B of the Act. In this Circular, the Information Technology Enabled Products/Services have been divided into fifteen categories, starting with Bank Office operations, Call centres etc. and ending with Website services. From the very description of such services, it is palpable that even though these fall under the overall ITES category, but some of them are quite different from each other. To cite, service at Sl.No. (vi) of this Circular is 'Geographic Information System services, and at Sl. No. (vii) is 'Human Resources Services.' No doubt, all these fifteen categories of products/services have been included under the major head of 'Information Technology Enabled Services' (ITES), but most of them are quite distinguishable from others. The fifteen broad categories set out in this Circular cannot per se be claimed as similar to each other. A cursory look at these products/services transpires that some of them are functionally quite different from each other. Further the level of investment required for providing such services is also not consistent. The mere fact that two services are placed under this category do not become automatically comparable. If a case providing one category of services under ITES is claimed as comparable with another in the category of service under ITES as per this circular, then it must be shown ex facie that it is broadly similar. Adverting to the facts of the instant case, the services rendered by Genesys fall under clause (vi) with the heading 'Geographical Information Systems Services', whereas those rendered by the assessee fall partly under clause (vii) with the heading 'Human Resources Services' and partly under clause (xi) with the heading 'Payroll'. On juxtaposition examination of these two sets of services, there is a vast difference which make one quite distinct from the other. In view of such functional incomparability between the assessee and Genesys, this company cannot be treated as comparable. Therefore, this case has to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 14.3]

Allocation of Unallocable Expenses

Certain companies included by the TPO in the final list of comparables under all the segments of the assessee, including software development segment, have been taken on segmental level. Common unallocated operating expenses of such companies were not taken into consideration in determining their respective profit margins. It is but natural that while calculating operating profit margin of such companies, effect of unallocated operating expenses qua relevant segments has to be given. It is so because the assessee's corresponding profit margin has been determined after considering all the relevant operating expenses and the comparison can be done only on level playing field. Therefore, the principle applied by the DRP was justified, that allocation of common unallocated expenses is required to be made. However, the view canvassed by the DRP that all such common unallocated expenses should be apportioned on the basis of segmental turnover to total turnover could not be subscribed. [Para 22]

Unallocated expenses obviously comprise several items of distinct nature and hence there cannot be a uniform key of apportionment. For example, `Rent' paid by an assessee cannot be bifurcated on the basis of sales or revenue from different segments, such as, Manufacturing, Trading and services. The extent of area used by each business segment varies as per the nature of transaction, which may have no relation with the gross revenue. For example, a manufacturing unit will need relatively more space than a trading unit. Similarly, a service unit will need still lesser space. In such a scenario, apportioning common rent expenditure on the basis of sales or gross revenue from such varied divisions, will give skewed results of segment profitability. Similarly, contribution of various segments to other items of expenses varies depending upon the nature of transaction, extent of capital employed and labour required etc. So all common expenses cannot be apportioned in the universal ratio of sales or gross revenue from different segments, each having its own separate features and characteristics. One can logically make allocation depending upon the nature of expenses and appropriate allocation key. As the assessee is not aggrieved by the otherwise inclusion of such companies on the ground of allocation of unallocated expenses, the impugned order is set aside and the Assessing Officer/TPO is to be directed to allocate common unallocated expenses on the basis of relevant keys as the case may be after allowing an opportunity of hearing to the assessee. [Para 23]

Considering the aforesaid factual differences, this company cannot be held to be comparable to a BPO service provider. [Para 105]

Comparable Infosys BPO Ltd.

This company is not only rendering a variety of services but it also owns significant intangibles. Further, it enjoys the goodwill and the brand value of the group which gives it more bargaining power and advantageous position with regard to pricing compared to a captive service provider like the assessee. Considering the aforesaid aspects, this company cannot be a comparable to a routine ITE service provider. [Para 108]

Comparable Datamatics Financial Services Ltd.

development segment by Tata Elxsi are not simply software development services but are complex in nature. The IPR in the form of software researched and developed were used as a tool for further development of software yielding higher margins. Thus, the segment of software development services in Tata Elxsi includes Design services including hardware design and, hence, is not comparable to simple software development services. [Para 5.5]

Comparables Indium Software (India) Ltd. and VMF Softech Ltd.: The assessee submitted that the TPO had wrongly excluded Indium presuming that the turnover of this company was less than one crore and further rejected VMF by citing information received under section 133(6) that the company was functioning on job work basis and that the predominant part of work was outsourced. The rectification application was filed under section 154 explaining how the turnover of Indium was incorrectly considered by the TPO presuming its turnover to be less than Rs. 1 crores but, in fact, it was Rs. 5.39 crores. Similarly, it was the contention of the assessee that the employee cost of VMF Softech was 53 per cent, which shows that the presumption of the TPO was incorrect. [Para 5.6]

The DRP upheld the conclusions of the TPO without citing any reasons. The department also did not point out any specific reasons to support the exclusion of these companies from the final list of comparable companies. Accordingly, it is directed that the TPO/Assessing Officer would decide the issue of inclusion of Indium/VMF Softech companies afresh after giving an opportunity of being heard to the assessee and considering all material placed before him for consideration. [Para 5.7]

As regards TCS-E serve Ltd., it is found that functions performed by TCS-E-Serve Ltd. included rendering of technical services like software testing etc., which required skilled persons. As far as the objection regarding related party transaction is concerned, the reasoning given by DRP that since this company was taken over by TCS group, therefore, there was no question of any separate details being given about related party transaction is correct. However, keeping in view the various factors, pointed out above this company cannot be taken as a comparable to the tested party. [Para 56]

As far as TCS-E-Serve International Ltd. is concerned, the assessee pointed out that as per the annual report, the functions performed by this company is to provide business process management services in banking and financial services verticals. It provides services comprising transaction process and technical services. Transaction processing includes processing, collections, customer care and payments in relation to the services by Citi Group to its corporate and retail clients. Technical services involve software testing, verification and validation of software at the time of implementation and data centre management activities. Segmental details for income from transactions processing services are not available in annual report. [Para 57]

It was found from records that the functions performed by this comparable are almost similar to that of TCS-E-Serve Ltd. and since this company is also rendering technical services and segmental details for income from transaction processing service are not available, therefore, this comparable has to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 59]

As regards Accentia Technology Ltd., assessee pointed out that this comparable provides high end functions such as knowledge processing outsourcing, legal process outsourcing, data process outsourcing, high end software services delivery besides offering software As A Service ("SaaS") Model in the healthcare outsourcing area. It also developed software products such as Business Process outsourcing management ('BPOM') solutions and HealthDox (HRCM Solution), apart from IT enabled services. Moreover, during FY 2009-10 a subsidiary of Accentia got amalgamated with the latter and the said extraordinary event has affected the overall profitability of Accentia. [Para 60]

It is clear from annual report that this company is primarily diversified knowledge process outsourcing company and coupled with the fact that extraordinary circumstance of amalgamation took place during the year, this comparable is directed to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 62]

As regards Infosys BPO Ltd., assessee pointed out that the functions performed by this company are high end integrated services assisting in improving competitive positioning and managing business processes in addition to providing increased value. The turnover of this company is Rs. 1127 crores as against Rs. 100 crores of ITeS segment of assessee. This company has brand ownership, which is evident from the brand related expenses incurred by this company of Rs. 69,16,780, whereas assessee does not have any brand or proprietary products. Further, offshore revenue, export income has not been specified separately. Therefore, it could not be found out as to whether export turnover is 75% of total income or not. Further, selling and marketing spend is 7% of revenue, which is not present in assessee's case. This company operates as a full Fledged risk taking entrepreneur whereas assessee is at minimal basis. [Para 63]

DRP has accepted the TPO's contention, inter alia, observing on the issue of brand ownership that creation of brand value is not on account of marketing expenses but because of superior services. DRP has observed that this service is given by employing better process and employees, therefore, the cost are higher on account of the same and most of the extra profits on account of brand value are set off because of the cost of this higher service. [Para 64]

These findings of DRP can't be accepted because it is not demonstrated as to what is the actual basis for these findings. The findings are purely on the basis of DRP's assumptions. As observed earlier, accepting assessee's plea that mere high turnover cannot be the basis for accepting or rejecting comparable, but coupled with the other dissimilarities the company is to be rejected. Therefore, following the Tribunal's decisions in the cases of Equant Solutions India (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2016] 66 taxmann.com 192/157 ITD 292 (Delhi - Trib.) and Bechtel India (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2016] 66 taxmann.com 6 (Delhi - Trib.), this comparable is excluded from list of comparables. [Para 65]

Turnover Filter

■

The controversy arises whether the companies having turnover exceeding Rs. 200 crores should be excluded while calculating the ALP of the assessee. [Para 19]

■

Based on the finding of the Tribunal in the case of Autodesk India Private Limited v. DCIT [2018] 96 taxmann.com 263 (Bangalore - Trib.), the companies having turnover exceeding Rs. 200 crores are excluded as comparable while calculating the ALP for the transactions international transactions carried out by the assessee with the AE. [Para 19.1]

■

Hence, the TPO/Assessing Officer is directed to exclude the companies from the list of comparable while calculating the ALP with respect to the international transaction carried out by the assessee if they are having turnover exceeding Rs. 200 crores after necessary verification. Accordingly, the ground of appeal of the assessee is hereby allowed. [Para 19.2]

Comparable Vitae International Accounting Services Pvt. Ltd.

■

The contention of the assessee that the said company is engaged in accounting, auditing and bookkeeping services is to be accepted. These activities are clearly distinct from the routine ITES/DCM services rendered by the assessee. Further, the company does not provide reliable segmental information to carve out margins relating to comparable services. In view of the functional dissimilarity and lack of segmental data and following the decision of the Hyderabad Tribunal in Infor (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [IT(TP)A No. 1341 (Hyd.) of 2024, dated 5-5-2025], it is to be held that Vitae International Accounting Services Pvt. Ltd. cannot be considered as a valid comparable and is liable to be excluded. [Para 36.1]

Comparables Domex E-Data Pvt. Ltd., Lagnaum Infotech Solutions Pvt. Ltd. and Brickworks India Pvt. Ltd.

■

With regard to Domex E-Data, Lagnaum Infotech Solutions and Brickworks India, it is noted that these companies are engaged in knowledge-based and analytics-driven services. The TPO himself has categorised the assessee's DCM segment as ITES. As per Rule 10TA(e) and 10TA(g) of the Incometax Rules, ITeS and KPO services are distinct in nature. Companies rendering KPO services, which involve higher skill, domain expertise and value addition, cannot be compared with a routine ITES service provider. It is further noted that Domex E-Data and Brickworks India do not have proper segmental information, and Brickworks India also earns abnormal profits. Lagnaum Infotech Solutions shows fluctuating margins over the years. These factors make the margins of these companies unreliable for benchmarking. Accordingly, these three companies are not suitable comparables and deserve to be excluded. [Para 36.2]

Comparable MPS Ltd.

■

It is found that this company is engaged in publishing solutions, digital learning content, platforms and related services. The activities involve content creation, full-service publishing, learning solutions and aggregation of content, which are clearly knowledge-intensive in nature. The Annual Report of MPS for financial year 2019-20 shows diversified operations across multiple verticals. The assessee, on the other hand, is a routine ITES service provider rendering low-end services. Therefore, MPS Ltd. fails the functional comparability test prescribed under Rule 10B of the Income Tax Rule. It is also note that there is no reliable segmental information available to isolate margins relatable to ITES activities. In similar facts, the Hyderabad Tribunal in Infor (India) (P.) Ltd. (supra) has held MPS is not comparable with an ITES provider. Following the same, the exclusion of MPS from the final set of comparables is directed. [Para 36.3]

■

In view of the above discussion, it is held that Vitae International Accounting Services, Domex E-Data, Lagnaum Infotech Solutions, MPS and Brickworks India are not comparable to the assessee in the DCM/ITeS segment. The Assessing Officer/TPO is directed to exclude these companies from the final list of comparables and recompute the arm's length price accordingly. Thus, the ground raised by the assessee on this issue is allowed. [Para 36.4]

Assessment year 2006-07

Comparable M/s. Datamatics Financial Services Ltd.

It is noted that the assessee has taken this company as one of the comparable for working out the ALP, but the TPO/DRP has disregarded the same considering that it is a loss incurring company and engaged in the different line of activity. However, the DRP rejected the same only on the reasoning that there were no segmental accounts available of the company. Thus, the issue arises whether non-availability of segmental accounts of comparable can be a reason for rejection? Admittedly, in the instant case, the significant receipt to the assessee is arising from the ITES, therefore this company can be considered as one of the comparable at entity level even in the absence of segmental data. Comparable Godrej Infotech Solutions Ltd/Tricom Infotech Solution Ltd.

Tax) [2013] 32 taxmann.com 21/57 SOT 14 (Hyd.-Trib.) has concluded that the directors of the company were involved in a fraud and the management of the company is tainted. [Para 11.5]

In view of the above, it is to be held that the above company cannot be taken as comparable for working out the ALP of the services rendered by the assessee to its AE. [Para 11.6]

+/- 5 per cent variation

Admittedly, the PLI of the assessee stands at 8.81 percent of operating profit/operating cost. Thus, the variation in the PLI declared by the assessee viz-a-viz the PLI of the comparable is less than 5 per cent, therefore the assessee is entitled for the benefit of proviso to section 92C. Comparable Vishal Technologies Ltd.

No doubt, assessee in the transfer pricing study has selected this company as a comparable. Even then, assessee's objection cannot be overruled for that reason alone. When the Transfer Pricing Officer has rejected the transfer pricing analysis of the assessee the department cannot use it selectively to their advantage. Moreover, it appears from the facts and materials placed on record that this company is different from the assessee considering the fact that it outsources its ITES to third party vendors. In other words, this company does not carry out the ITES activities itself but gets it done through others. This is evident from low employee cost of the company. Compared to the aforesaid practice of this company, the assessee claims to have carried out the ITES activities all by itself, thereby, has incurred a comparatively higher employee cost.

The Assessing Officer/TPO is directed to examine this aspect by verifying the annual report of the company and other relevant documents and if assessee's claim of low employee cost of this company is found to be correct, this company should not be treated as comparable. [Para 61]

HCL Comnet Systems & Services Ltd. and Information Technologies India Ltd. :

These companies were found to be having more than 15 per cent Related Party Transactions (RPT). Accordingly, the Assessing Officer/TPO is directed to exclude these companies from the set of comparables. [Para 9.1]

Infosys Ltd.

It is clear from the finding of this Tribunal in the case of Ariba Technologies India (P.) Ltd. (supra), this company is deriving revenue from the software product and has a huge intangible assets apart from the brand value and a leader in the market. Accordingly, the Assessing Officer/TPO is directed to exclude this company from the list of comparables. [Para 10]

Mold-tek Technology Ltd. (Seg.)

The functional comparability has been considered by this Tribunal in a series of decision including the decision of Special Bench in the case of Maersk Global Centres (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2014] 43 taxmann.com 100/147 ITD 83 (Mum.-Trib). The co-ordinate bench of this Tribunal in the case of Ariba Technologies India (P.) Ltd. (supra) has held that this company is engaged in the engineering services being the nature of producing designs, drawings, detailed structure of engineering drawings using 2D and 3D software could not be compared with the assessee and consequently the Assessing Officer/TPO is directed to exclude this company from the set of comparables. [Para 12.1]

Accentia Technology Ltd.

The assessee has submitted that there is an extraordinary event of amalgamation during the year under consideration. [Para 13.1]

There is no dispute that amalgamation, merger or acquisition is considered as extraordinary event for the purpose of considering a particular entity as comparable. The co-ordinate bench of this Tribunal in the case of Sony Mobile Communications International AB v. Dy. CIT [2016] 69 taxmann.com 404 (Delhi) held that once acquisition and merger etc. has taken place, it is always likely to affect the profitability of such a company in the year of acquisition etc. There cannot be any standard yardstick to measure the impact of such a factor on the overall profitability of such a company.

Therefore, for limited purpose of considering the said record, this issue is set aside to the record of Assessing Officer/TPO and then decide the issue of comparability of this company in the light of the above observations. [Para 13.3]

Vishal Information Technology Ltd.

The comparability of this company has been examined by this Tribunal in the case of Ariba Technologies India Ltd. (supra), it was found that this company was outsourcing its job and therefore it fails the employee cost filter.
